Scenario: Back up the RMM before testing
Before you start: Server administrator; current deployment working
Steps to perform:
1. Run scripts/backup-database.py using the documented deployment procedure.
2. Record the backup location and date.
3. Confirm a non-empty backup exists.
Expected result: Database backup exists. Keep it outside the active application data folder as well.

Before you start: One spare Windows PC; administrator login
Steps to perform:
1. Use a spare PC or disposable VM.
2. Create a QA Test customer/company and group.
3. Record browser, RMM version/commit and PC name in Start Here.
4. Use test mail and files.
Expected result: Tests use a separate QA scope; no production customer records, backups or devices are deleted.

Before you start: Existing administrator credentials
Steps to perform:
1. Sign in.
2. Confirm Dashboard loads.
3. Sign out.
4. Try opening the previous page.
5. Sign back in.
Expected result: Valid credentials work. Signed-out API requests require sign-in. Do not record passwords.

Before you start: Signed in
Steps to perform:
1. Open Backups and refresh.
2. Repeat on Tickets and User Management.
3. Use browser Back and Forward.
Expected result: Refresh retains an allowed page. Back/Forward changes pages correctly.

Before you start: Desktop browser and phone or narrow browser
Steps to perform:
1. Open Dashboard, Computers, Tickets and User Management.
2. Test at phone width.
3. Open an Add/Edit dialog.
4. Confirm fields and buttons remain reachable.
Expected result: Cards and dialogs are usable. Tables may scroll inside their container; page controls remain accessible.

Before you start: Administrator; QA scope
Steps to perform:
1. Add customer QA Test with a test contact.
2. Add QA Test Company linked to that customer.
3. Refresh.
Expected result: Correct customer/company link and contact details persist.

Before you start: QA customer/company
Steps to perform:
1. Edit test contact, email and phone.
2. Save and refresh.
Expected result: Updated values persist without creating duplicate records.

Before you start: QA company
Steps to perform:
1. Add QA Lab location.
2. Add QA Windows group within it.
3. Rename the test group.
4. Refresh.
Expected result: Location/group belong to the correct company; rename persists.

Before you start: Spare Windows PC; QA group; trusted installer source
Steps to perform:
1. Add Device and select QA company/location/group.
2. Generate enrollment link.
3. Install agent on the spare PC.
4. Wait for synchronization.
Expected result: Computer appears under the selected company/location/group. Agent connects; existing customer devices are unaffected.

Before you start: QA PC enrolled
Steps to perform:
1. Confirm Online.
2. Shut down/disconnect only the QA PC.
3. Wait at least one 30-second inventory refresh.
4. Reconnect it.
Expected result: State changes Offline then Online after fresh synchronization. Device record remains visible.

Before you start: QA Windows PC online
Steps to perform:
1. Open Computers.
2. Wait for CPU, memory and system-disk readings.
3. Compare disk/memory with Windows tools at approximately the same time.
Expected result: Measured values and reading time appear. Transient CPU variation is normal. Unknown readings are not shown as healthy zeroes.

Before you start: QA PC
Steps to perform:
1. Rename its RMM display name.
2. Refresh the page.
Expected result: Name persists and the computer remains linked to its company/group.

Before you start: QA and existing inventory
Steps to perform:
1. Search for QA PC.
2. Select QA company.
3. Clear filters.
Expected result: Matching records appear; filters clear without losing records.

Before you start: QA company/group contains the QA PC
Steps to perform:
1. Attempt to delete the non-empty QA company/group.
2. Cancel where appropriate.
3. Create and delete a separate empty temporary group/customer.
Expected result: Non-empty records are protected. Eligible empty temporary records can be removed. MeshCentral groups are not silently deleted.

Before you start: Administrator; disposable employee login
Steps to perform:
1. Add QA Backup Tech with a unique initial password.
2. Choose Technician.
3. Allow Backups: Manage and Antivirus: View only; leave other features No access.
4. Save.
Expected result: User card shows exactly those permissions. Password is not displayed back. Keep admin signed in separately.

Before you start: QA Backup Tech initial credentials
Steps to perform:
1. Open a private browser.
2. Sign in as QA Backup Tech.
3. Confirm password-change prompt.
4. Set a new password of at least 16 characters.
Expected result: Workspace is unavailable until personal password is set. New password works; initial password no longer works.

Before you start: QA Backup Tech signed in
Steps to perform:
1. Confirm only Backups and Security navigation is available.
2. Enter /#users, /#providers and /#devices in the address bar.
Expected result: Restricted pages are not shown. Navigation falls back to an allowed page. Menus alone are not the full security test; complete T018 too.

Before you start: QA Backup Tech; browser Developer Tools Network
Steps to perform:
1. In the signed-in private browser address bar open /api/users, /api/provider-registry and /api/patches.
2. Observe HTTP responses.
3. Return to the RMM.
Expected result: Each forbidden endpoint returns HTTP 403 without records or vendor settings. Do not paste cookies or tokens into evidence.

Before you start: QA Backup Tech; Antivirus View only
Steps to perform:
1. Open Security.
2. Confirm status/preferences can be read.
3. Look for Edit provider, Remove choice and Configure console.
Expected result: RMM change buttons are hidden; restricted mutation requests are denied. External vendor consoles use their own permissions.

Before you start: Admin can edit QA Backup Tech; separate admin session
Steps to perform:
1. Grant Computers: Manage to the QA employee.
2. Sign in again.
3. Generate a QA enrollment link and edit QA computer name.
4. Leave Remote access disabled.
Expected result: Computer operations work only after grant; remote Connect remains unavailable without its separate permission.

Before you start: QA employee has Computers access; QA PC online
Steps to perform:
1. As admin grant Remote access: Manage.
2. Employee signs in again.
3. Open Connect.
4. Revoke Remote access and sign in again.
Expected result: RMM provides Connect only with remote permission. MeshCentral independently checks its own login/rights; RMM does not create MeshCentral accounts.

Before you start: Existing admin and QA employee
Steps to perform:
1. As admin open Providers, AI Agents, email setup and User Management.
2. Confirm QA employee cannot open those settings.
Expected result: Settings are administrator-only even when employee has Backup/Antivirus Manage permission.

Before you start: QA employee signed in; admin in different browser
Steps to perform:
1. As admin remove an employee permission and save.
2. In the old employee tab trigger a server-backed action or refresh.
3. Sign in again.
Expected result: Old session is rejected; new session reflects revised permissions. Previously accepted in-progress jobs may finish.

Before you start: Disposable QA employee; retain administrator session
Steps to perform:
1. As admin uncheck Account active and save.
2. Employee refreshes or triggers an action.
3. Attempt employee sign-in.
4. Reactivate for later testing.
Expected result: Existing session is rejected on next request. Inactive user cannot sign in.

Before you start: Disposable QA employee
Steps to perform:
1. Reset employee password in Edit User.
2. Confirm old employee session/password no longer work.
3. Sign in with new initial password.
Expected result: Reset requires another personal password change before workspace access.

Before you start: Main admin; never disable your only working account
Steps to perform:
1. Open your own admin Edit form.
2. Attempt to deactivate yourself or change your role to Technician.
3. Confirm rejection and leave account unchanged.
Expected result: Self-deactivation/self-demotion is rejected. At least one active administrator must remain.

Before you start: QA PC online; authorized MeshCentral login; Remote access permission
Steps to perform:
1. Click Connect on QA PC.
2. Authenticate with MeshCentral as needed.
3. Open desktop and perform a harmless action.
4. Disconnect.
Expected result: Correct PC opens. Remote input/display works. Other computers are not connected accidentally.

Before you start: Scripts feature access
Steps to perform:
1. Search Disk Space Report.
2. View Code.
3. Copy it.
4. Download the script.
Expected result: The same script content is visible, copied and downloaded. Marketplace does not remotely execute it.

Before you start: QA PC; downloaded Disk Space Report; reviewed source
Steps to perform:
1. Inspect script before running.
2. Follow existing instructions for trusted PowerShell files.
3. Run Disk Space Report locally.
4. Record output.
Expected result: Report lists real drive data without deleting files or changing the PC. Respect company execution-policy requirements.

Before you start: Administrator; known provider console addresses
Steps to perform:
1. Review/add Acronis, Comet and MSP360 backup choices and required antivirus choices.
2. Edit a test provider note.
3. Refresh.
Expected result: Provider metadata persists. Adding a provider alone does not connect its API or install an agent.

Before you start: Admin; supported Acronis API setup if available
Steps to perform:
1. Save supported credentials through Provider Setup.
2. Reopen Edit and leave secret blank.
3. Save an unrelated note.
4. Inspect browser response for returned fields.
Expected result: Saved secret is never returned; leaving it blank preserves it. Do not include actual secrets in screenshots or Issues.

Before you start: QA company; Backup/Security Manage permission
Steps to perform:
1. Assign backup provider to QA company.
2. Assign antivirus provider.
3. Refresh and filter by provider.
Expected result: Company choices persist. No installation or protection is claimed solely because a preference was saved.

Before you start: Acronis test tenant; API client access; existing QA protected device
Steps to perform:
1. Test Acronis connection.
2. Load inventory.
3. Link QA PC to the matching Acronis resource.
4. Compare company/device identities carefully.
Expected result: Authentication succeeds; matching device is linked uniquely. Missing/ambiguous backup evidence stays unverified.

Before you start: QA PC and backup plan in Acronis console
Steps to perform:
1. Run a backup in Acronis for QA PC.
2. Wait for completion.
3. Refresh RMM backup history.
4. Check task identity and result.
Expected result: Vendor confirms completed backup. RMM reports only supported, uniquely matched task evidence. No completed task is treated as proof of retained recovery points.

Before you start: Completed QA backup; harmless test file; alternate restore folder
Steps to perform:
1. Select a backed-up QA test file in vendor console.
2. Restore it to a NEW folder.
3. Open file and compare content.
Expected result: File restores correctly to alternate location. Do not overwrite production files or restore an entire production disk.

Before you start: Chosen vendor test account, agent/license/storage as required
Steps to perform:
1. Assign chosen provider in RMM.
2. Open its console with vendor-authorized credentials.
3. Run backup and test-file restore there.
4. Record vendor result separately.
Expected result: Vendor backup/restore works if configured. RMM console-only integration remains explicitly unverified; do not mark native RMM API automation as passed.

Before you start: QA PC; chosen licensed antivirus provider
Steps to perform:
1. Check protection/update status in vendor console.
2. Confirm antivirus and MeshCentral agent remain running.
3. Restart QA PC and reconnect.
4. Review vendor alerts/quarantine if connection fails.
Expected result: Vendor verifies protection; MeshCentral still connects. RMM preference alone does not prove protection. Investigate detections rather than disabling all protection.

Scenario: Create and edit a real patch record
Before you start: QA PC; Windows Update pending list or vendor applicability guidance
Steps to perform:
1. Choose a REAL pending/applicable update on QA PC.
2. Add exact KB/reference, description, vendor, type/severity.
3. Set Requires Reboot based on vendor guidance.
4. Edit and refresh.
Expected result: Catalog fields persist. Previously installed KBs are not used as evidence of a needed patch. Catalog does not discover/install updates automatically.

Scenario: Patch search, categories and reboot label
Before you start: QA patch record
Steps to perform:
1. Search exact patch name/ID.
2. Filter its type.
3. Toggle Requires Reboot in Edit and save.
Expected result: Correct patch is found and declared reboot setting is displayed accurately.

Before you start: QA company; online QA Windows PCs with signed-in test users
Steps to perform:
1. Deploy/plan notice for QA company only.
2. Enter a real maintenance date/time including time zone.
3. Check each signed-in QA user session for the popup.
4. Record per-PC delivery and screenshots.
Expected result: Signed-in test sessions receive planned-update notice with declared reboot requirement. Windows accepted is not proof user read it. No patch install/restart is implied.

Before you start: QA company; one disconnected QA PC
Steps to perform:
1. Keep one QA PC offline.
2. Submit a QA notice.
3. Inspect per-PC results.
Expected result: Offline/busy/failed/uncertain targets are shown honestly rather than claiming delivery to all PCs. Verify actual screens for online targets.

Before you start: QA maintenance window; approved applicable update
Steps to perform:
1. Install applicable update using Windows Update or authorized vendor workflow.
2. Restart only if required and agreed.
3. Check Windows Update history/build afterward.
4. Record actual result.
Expected result: Windows/vendor confirms installation. RMM planned count is not treated as verified installed state. Native installation remains Future Features.

Before you start: QA/owned subnet; online Windows scan agent; consent to scan
Steps to perform:
1. Run ipconfig on QA scan agent.
2. Identify active adapter address/mask.
3. Enter its actual private subnet, e.g. 192.168.0.0/24 only if matching.
4. Select QA company/agent and scan.
5. Wait for completion.
Expected result: Real observed devices appear; source agent/subnet are correct. Do not scan arbitrary customer/public networks.

Before you start: Completed QA scan
Steps to perform:
1. Compare two discovered IPs with known QA devices/router.
2. Filter device types.
3. Edit a QA device label/type.
4. Refresh.
Expected result: Observed IP/port data matches evidence; manual labels persist. Discovery map does not invent physical network topology.

Before you start: QA scan setup
Steps to perform:
1. Try a subnet that is NOT connected to the selected QA agent, or an invalid CIDR.
2. Submit scan.
Expected result: Validation/error explains the problem. It does not invent successful results. Do not repeatedly start scans on a busy agent.

Before you start: QA domain; DC/domain-joined agent; RSAT; authorized service account
Steps to perform:
1. Select QA company and AD-capable agent.
2. Sync from AD.
3. Compare known test user/group/OU with AD tools.
Expected result: Real directory records appear in correct scope. No AD accounts, passwords or memberships are changed. If prerequisites missing, mark Blocked or justified Not applicable.

Before you start: QA customer/company and PC
Steps to perform:
1. Create QA ticket with title, description, customer, PC, priority/category.
2. Open its details.
3. Refresh.
Expected result: Unique ticket number, correct relationships and data persist.

Before you start: QA manual ticket; Tickets Manage
Steps to perform:
1. Add internal note.
2. Edit priority/category.
3. Mark In Progress, then Resolved.
4. Reopen it.
Expected result: Status and notes persist; note identifies actual signed-in technician. Internal notes are not emailed.

Scenario: Configure a dedicated test support mailbox
Before you start: Admin; IMAP mailbox/server; verified TLS; provider instructions
Steps to perform:
1. Configure test address, host, user, folder and password.
2. Save and run Check Mail.
3. Reopen setup.
Expected result: Connection succeeds with verified TLS. Password remains masked. Initial connection establishes new-mail checkpoint rather than importing historical inbox.

Before you start: Configured test mailbox; Check Mail checkpoint completed
Steps to perform:
1. Send a NEW message from a separate test sender after setup.
2. Wait for poll or Check Mail.
3. Open created ticket.
Expected result: One ticket is created with correct subject/body/requester and email source. Attachments remain in mailbox; no outbound acknowledgment is expected.

Before you start: QA email-created ticket
Steps to perform:
1. Reply in original email thread from same test sender.
2. Check mail twice.
3. Resolve ticket, then send another reply.
Expected result: Reply appends once to the same ticket; repeat checks do not duplicate it. New reply reopens resolved ticket when properly threaded.

Before you start: Configured test mailbox; new unmatched test address
Steps to perform:
1. Send new mail from an address not stored in contacts.
2. Open ticket and inspect customer assignment.
Expected result: Ticket remains unmatched/unassigned rather than guessed. Saved email match is not proof of sender identity.

Before you start: Admin; supported provider API account/key; small API usage budget
Steps to perform:
1. Add chosen AI provider, model and key.
2. Test Connection.
3. Select default agent.
4. Reopen Edit.
Expected result: Supported model authenticates and returns structured output. Key is masked. API billing is separate from ChatGPT subscription; do not record keys.

Before you start: QA ticket; configured default AI; Tickets Manage
Steps to perform:
1. Review ticket text for sensitive data.
2. Run AI Review on a harmless QA problem.
3. Read summary, causes, steps/questions.
Expected result: Structured suggestions appear with agent/model information. No commands run, no ticket is auto-resolved, and suggestions require technician review.

Before you start: Default AI has automatic email review enabled
Steps to perform:
1. Send new harmless QA ticket email.
2. Wait for review job.
3. Edit ticket or add note after review.
4. Review again.
Expected result: Automatic review appears or a clear job error is shown. Changed ticket content invalidates old analysis; fresh review reflects latest information.

Scenario: Enable and save an offline rule
Before you start: QA PC; Monitoring Manage; QA company; existing rules initially disabled
Steps to perform:
1. Edit Computer offline rule.
2. Scope to QA company.
3. Set duration 1 minute; enable; optionally enable auto-ticket.
4. Save and refresh.
Expected result: Save works, settings persist, and unrelated companies are not included. Non-percentage rules are not blocked by hidden fields.

Before you start: Enabled QA offline rule; QA PC initially online
Steps to perform:
1. Disconnect only QA PC.
2. Wait for fresh inventory and sustained duration (allow several minutes).
3. Check Monitoring alerts and Tickets.
4. Run another check.
Expected result: One active alert and, if opted in, one automatic ticket appear. Repeat checks do not create duplicates for same incident.

Scenario: Recovery does not close technician ticket
Before you start: Active QA offline alert with ticket
Steps to perform:
1. Reconnect QA PC.
2. Wait for fresh inventory/check.
3. Inspect alert and ticket.
Expected result: Alert becomes Recovered from fresh evidence. Recovery note is added; ticket stays open until technician resolves it.

Before you start: QA Windows PC; choose safe measurable condition; no stress test on production
Steps to perform:
1. Create QA CPU/memory/disk rule with suitable threshold/recovery and 1-minute duration.
2. Check fresh readings and pending evidence.
3. Observe alert only if condition stays breached.
Expected result: Rule uses measured fresh evidence and hysteresis. No alert appears merely from a single spike or repeatedly cached timestamp.

Before you start: QA Windows PC; Spooler present; do not stop production services
Steps to perform:
1. Add a QA service rule for Spooler.
2. Check known running state.
3. If safe in isolated QA VM, stop it locally, observe sustained alert, then restart locally.
Expected result: RMM reads service state; it does not change the service. Alert/recovery follow fresh evidence and duration.

Scenario: Unknown/busy data does not imply failure
Before you start: QA metric/service rule; QA agent temporarily unavailable
Steps to perform:
1. Temporarily disconnect QA agent or observe a reported busy/unknown read.
2. Inspect Pending / Unavailable Readings.
3. Restore connection.
Expected result: Unknown/stale readings do not create metric/service failure tickets or falsely recover an existing alert. Offline rule is evaluated separately.

Before you start: Active QA alert
Steps to perform:
1. Acknowledge alert.
2. Refresh and check linked ticket.
Expected result: Alert becomes Acknowledged, not Recovered. Ticket is not silently resolved.

Before you start: Supported Acronis integration; uniquely linked QA resource/task; controlled test failure if available
Steps to perform:
1. Add QA Acronis unsuccessful-backup rule.
2. Compare evaluated task/resource with vendor console.
3. If no confirmed failure exists, record coverage as unknown/no failure rather than forcing a production failure.
Expected result: Only uniquely linked confirmed failed task evidence can trigger a backup alert. Missing/ambiguous tasks are unverified. Full failure-trigger test may be Blocked.

Before you start: Admin; QA records created; safe maintenance window
Steps to perform:
1. Record QA account permissions, device/group, ticket, provider choice and rule.
2. Restart only maldoori using documented PM2 command.
3. Sign in again and compare.
Expected result: Records/settings remain. In-memory sessions require sign-in again. New account password changes survive restart; environment bootstrap does not reset them.

Before you start: Database backup; separate disposable RMM instance; do not overwrite live DB
Steps to perform:
1. Restore backup into a SEPARATE test instance using documented procedure.
2. Start it with appropriate test integrations disabled or isolated.
3. Verify representative records and admin sign-in.
Expected result: Recovery restores usable data/accounts. Production stays unchanged; no duplicate scheduled actions or email intake are allowed from rehearsal instance.

Before you start: Droplet metrics; several QA PCs; typical technician actions
Steps to perform:
1. Observe CPU/RAM/disk/network while refreshing inventory and using one scan/remote session.
2. Record device count, concurrent sessions, response times and errors.
3. Check for sustained memory/CPU pressure.
Expected result: Measured baseline is documented. Small QA success does not prove 100-device capacity; larger load test remains separate.

Scenario: Clean up QA settings and review release
Before you start: Admin; complete or recorded outcomes
Steps to perform:
1. Disable temporary monitoring rules.
2. Deactivate test employees.
3. Cancel vendor test schedules if appropriate.
4. Keep useful test evidence/history.
5. Review all Critical failures and Blocked scenarios.
Expected result: No unintended QA jobs remain. Required critical tests pass; unresolved risks are documented before customer rollout. Do not delete production backups or records.
